how: Reported as a barrier element after the cement job gave poor bonding
summary: The cement above the Sele Formation bonded poorly. The completion report states that the green clay above Sele and the cement above the reservoir now act as barrier elements against the reservoir.

how: Ultrasonic and bond log run in 2009 to confirm the Green Clay as a barrier
summary: The log found a very high content of solids in the annulus through the whole Green Clay interval (2,200 to 2,850 m along the hole) and further up, and suggests that other formations have also collapsed against the casing.

how: Plugging programme that expects the seal and plans a log to check it
summary: The programme says the Green Clay has collapsed around the 13 3/8 inch casing and made a seal on all but one well so far, and expects the same here. The result of the log is not in the open reports.

how: Pressure test to 32 bar through a cut in the casing to qualify the clay
summary: The programme plans to pressure test through holes in the 13 3/8 inch casing to qualify the green clay as a barrier element, and lists at least 300 m of it in the barrier drawing. The result is not in the open reports.

how: Total loss of mud while milling a window in uncemented casing
summary: 792 m of Green Clay lay open behind uncemented 13 3/8 inch casing. It was assumed to have collapsed around the casing in the two years since the casing was set, but total losses showed communication up to the 18 5/8 inch shoe.

how: Bond log from 1987 used in the plugging programme
summary: The bond log shows very good formation bonding outside the 9 5/8 inch casing in the Hordaland Group from 1,566 to 1,962 m along the hole. The programme lists formation bonding as a barrier element to be verified by log.

how: Plugging programme with formation bonding as the first choice
summary: The Sele Formation is to be plugged back inside the casing if a log finds enough formation bonding above it. The result is not in the open reports.

unit: Rogaland or Hordaland Gp above the Lista Fm
how: Ultrasonic and bond log during plugging
summary: The log showed formation bonding good enough for permanent plugging against the Lista Formation, in two intervals. The interval was not pressure tested.

unit: Shale above the Lysing and Nise formations
how: Ultrasonic and bond log during plugging
summary: 80 m of formation collapse above the Lysing Formation and 126 m above the Nise Formation were confirmed by log and drawn as barrier elements.

how: Leak test through a cut in the 9 5/8 inch casing
phrase: qualified as barrier for the P
summary: Another report states that the Shetland Group was qualified as a barrier in this well by leak testing through a cut in the casing at 3,100 m along the hole.

how: Qualification cited by a later plugging programme
summary: A later programme for a neighbouring well states that collapsed Hordaland formation was qualified as a barrier in this well.

how: Plugging programme that relies on earlier qualifications
summary: The programme plans to use collapsed Hordaland and Shetland formation as barriers if the logs show it, based on qualifications in two other Snorre wells. The result is not in the open reports.
The programme plans to log for collapsed formation behind the 13 3/8 inch casing and to test it as a barrier if it is there. The result is not in the open reports.

how: Bond log and risk register for the plugging
summary: The well was chosen for a test of the Shetland Group as a barrier. The risk register records that the Shetland formation had not collapsed or that the log data were poor, and the bond log rates 2,170 to 2,246 m along the hole as poor with low potential for isolation.

how: Study that depends on the test in 33/9-L-4 H
summary: A study says the middle part of the Shetland Group can be qualified as a barrier from 2,181 m vertical depth if the test in 33/9-L-4 H is good.
